```{r}
         regular = "C:/Users/sarae/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts/AtkinsonHyperlegibleMono-Regular.ttf") # The full path must be specified for R to successfully locate the font. You can find a copy of AtkinsonHyperlegibleMono-Regular.ttf in the font folder in the analysis_quant folder. I haven't tried specifying the path that way instead of going the system fonts route.
```

# Loading in data
```{r}
# Traditional data csv
dat_trad <- read_survey(file_name = "data/AIandNDSurvey_June_18_2025_02.49.csv")

# Prolific data csv
dat_prol <- read_survey(
  file_name = "data/AIandNDSurvey_Prolific_June_18_2025_02.49.csv",
  legacy = TRUE #without this, there's an error loading in the file
  )
  
```


## Extracting the "Prefer not to say" answers for "Are you neurodivergent?":

```{r}
# For the non-Prolific answers (which we're interested in removing):
dat_trad_prefNOT <- dat_trad %>%
  filter(neurodivergent == "Prefer not to say") #it looks like only the test/preview answers say "Prefer not to say"

dat_trad_prefNOT

excl_prefNOT_n <- 0 # set this manually


# For the prolific answers (which are already screened so even if participants say "Prefer not to say" we know they've already answered yes to being neurodivergent in the screener):
dat_prol_prefNOT <- dat_prol %>%
  filter(neurodivergent == "Prefer not to say") # 4 actual responses (NOT test/preview) say "Prefer not to say"

dat_prol_prefNOT

```



# Cleaning the data for:
- including only those who consented
- including only those who completed the study
- excluding preview/test responses
- removing ALL responses if duplicate IDs were found (for the columns: ResponseId, Q29 and PROLIFIC_PID)
- excluded any rows where ALL of the columns (12 to 49, i.e. AI_Tools_List_1 to anything_else) are empty/NA

```{r}
# Cleaning the data:
dat_trad_clean <- dat_trad %>%
  filter(consent_form == "Yes, I have read the Participant Information Sheet, Privacy Notice and Consent Form and AGREE to take part in this study.") %>% ## Selecting only those that consented to partaking in the study
  filter(Progress == 100) %>% ## Filtering out those that don't have 100% Progress
  filter(DistributionChannel != "preview") %>% ## Filtering out those that are previews (i.e. test responses, not actual responses)
  filter(Status == "IP Address") %>% ## Filtering out the Survey Previews
  filter(Finished == TRUE) %>% ## Filtering out those that are unfinished
  group_by(ResponseId) %>%
  filter(n() == 1) %>%  # Keep only IDs that appear exactly once (NO DUPLICATES)
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(if_any(AI_Tools_List_1:anything_else, ~ !is.na(.) & . != "")) # Removes any rows where all of those columns (AI_Tools_List_1 to anything_else) are empty/NA


dat_prol_clean <- dat_prol %>%
  filter(consent_form == "Yes, I have read the Participant Information Sheet, Privacy Notice and Consent Form and AGREE to take part in this study.") %>% ## Selecting only those that consented to partaking in the study
  filter(Progress == 100) %>% ## Filtering out those that don't have 100% Progress
  filter(DistributionChannel != "preview") %>% ## Filtering out those that are previews (i.e. test responses, not actual responses)
  filter(Status == "IP Address") %>% ## Filtering out the Survey Previews
  filter(Finished == TRUE) %>% ## Filtering out those that are unfinished
  group_by(ResponseId) %>%
  filter(n() == 1) %>%  # Keep only IDs that appear exactly once (NO DUPLICATES)
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(if_any(AI_Tools_List_1:anything_else, ~ !is.na(.) & . != "")) %>% # Removes any rows where all of those columns (AI_Tools_List_1 to anything_else) are empty/NA
  group_by(Q29) %>%
  filter(n() == 1) %>%  # Keep only IDs that appear exactly once (NO DUPLICATES)
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(PROLIFIC_PID) %>%
  filter(n() == 1) %>%  # Keep only IDs that appear exactly once (NO DUPLICATES)
  ungroup()

```

### Count of exclusions at each stage (trad AND prolific):
```{r}
# Stats of n excluded according to what reason (trad then prolific):
excl_raw_n <- trad_raw_n + prol_raw_n 
excl_raw_n # n raw data responses
excl_raw_removals <- 0

## + Filtering to exclude "Prefer not to say" responses from trad data:
excl_prefNOT <- excl_raw_n - excl_prefNOT_n # n left, after prefNOT exclusions

## + Filtering to exclude preview/test responses:
excl_prev <- trad_excl_prev + prol_excl_prev # n left, after preview/test exclusions
excl_prev_n <- excl_raw_n - excl_prev
excl_prev_n # n removed due to preview/test exclusions

## + Filtering to only include those who consented:
excl_con <- trad_excl_con + prol_excl_con # n left, after consent exclusions
excl_con_n <- excl_prev - excl_con
excl_con_n # n removed due to consent exclusions

## + Filtering to ONLY include finished responses:
excl_fin <- trad_excl_fin + prol_excl_fin # n left, after finished exclusions
excl_fin_n <- excl_con - excl_fin
excl_fin_n # n removed due to finished exclusions

## + Removing any rows where all of those columns (AI_Tools_List_1 to anything_else) are empty/NA:
excl_NA <- trad_excl_NA + prol_excl_NA # n left, after NA exclusions
excl_NA_n <- excl_fin - excl_NA
excl_NA_n # n removed due to NA exclusions

## + Filtering to exclude duplicate responses:
excl_dup <- trad_excl_dup + prol_excl_dup  # n left, after duplicate exclusions
excl_dup_n <- excl_NA - excl_dup
excl_dup_n # n removed due to duplicate exclusions


## + Manually checking if there's any unusual uniformity in participant responses (i.e. if someone went through and just picked the same answer to everything to speed through the survey) + if the Part 1 and Part 2 survey answers match logically (e.g. a mismatch is if someone say they rarely/never use AI, but then in Part 2 mention they use it.)
excl_unif_n <- 0 # n removed due to uniformity/mismatch exclusions
excl_unif <- excl_dup - excl_unif_n # n left, after uniformity/mismatch exclusions

```


### Table of exclusions at each stage:
```{r}
excl_count <- tibble(
  order = 0:7,
  description = c(
    "Raw data",
    "Including only neurodivergent responses",
    "Removing preview/test responses",
    "Including only those who consented to participation",
    "Including only completed responses",
    "Removing empty/NA responses",
    "Removing duplicate responses",
    "Removing suspiciously uniform/mismatched responses"
  ),
  n_removed = c(
    excl_raw_removals,
    excl_prefNOT_n,
    excl_prev_n,
    excl_con_n,
    excl_fin_n,
    excl_NA_n,
    excl_dup_n,
    excl_unif_n
  ),
  n_left = c(
    excl_raw_n,
    excl_prefNOT,
    excl_prev,
    excl_con,
    excl_fin,
    excl_NA,
    excl_dup,
    excl_unif
  )
)

excl_count

```



# Wide to Long
```{r}
# Pivoting from wide to long:
dat_trad_long <- dat_trad_clean %>%
  mutate(across(-c(ResponseId), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(ResponseId),
    names_to = "Question",
    values_to = "Answer"
  )


dat_prol_long <- dat_prol_clean %>%
  mutate(across(-c(ResponseId), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(ResponseId),
    names_to = "Question",
    values_to = "Answer"
  )

```


# Combining data sets
```{r}
# Combining the two data sets, but labelling which IDs come from which:

dat_comb <- bind_rows(
  dat_trad_long %>% mutate(Recruitment = "Traditional"),
  dat_prol_long %>% mutate(Recruitment = "Prolific")
) %>%
  select(ResponseId, Recruitment, everything())

dat_comb



# Combining the wide format trad and prol data:

dat_wide_comb <- dat_comb %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Question,
              values_from = Answer)

dat_wide_comb

```


# Matching IDs with the qual dataset:
```{r}
# To clarify, cleaned and combined data from this Rmarkdown was used for the qualitative analysis. During that analysis, IDs were added (to make them easier to identify than just purely using ResponseIds), and open-text responses were judged for if they seemed written by generative AI rather than the participants, using interrater agreement. So here I'm backtracking and taking the IDs produced during the qual analysis and adding them to the combined dataset here.
# To do this, I downloaded demos.csv (last modified on 3 July 2025 by Jade Burke):
dat_qual_IDs <- read_csv("data/demos.csv") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Question,
              values_from = Answer) %>%
  select(Pseudonym, ResponseId)

dat_qual_IDs


# Adding qual IDs to matching ResponseId in dat_wide_comb
dat_wide_comb <- inner_join(dat_qual_IDs, dat_wide_comb, by = "ResponseId") # beware that you have to rerun the "Combining the wide format trad and prol data" bit above this first before running just this bit of code on its own, otherwise if you keep rerunning just this bit you'll get lots of repeated rows that'll keep growing each time like a clone army.

dat_wide_comb


# Making sure dat_comb has the qual IDs:
dat_comb <- dat_wide_comb %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Pseudonym, ResponseId, Recruitment),
    names_to = "Question",
    values_to = "Answer"
  )

```


# Removing suspicous IDs (identified as AI by Jade Burke & Helena Paterson via interrater agreement assessment):
```{r}
# from the "demos" tab in the "selected_questions - SS coding" XLSX file in the analysis_open_responses folder:

# Flagged IDs from qual data for removal: ID15, ID21, ID30, ID53, ID8 (5 responses total removed from quant and qual analysis)
dat_comb <- dat_comb %>%
  filter(
    !Pseudonym %in% c(
      "Participant_15",
      "Participant_21",
      "Participant_30",
      "Participant_53",
      "Participant_8"
    ))


dat_wide_comb <- dat_wide_comb %>%
  filter(
    !Pseudonym %in% c(
      "Participant_15",
      "Participant_21",
      "Participant_30",
      "Participant_53",
      "Participant_8"
    ))

```


### Adding this as a stage in the exclusions count table:
MAKE SURE to restart R session and outputs, because if you don't and keep re-running the code, there will be lots of duplicate rows.

```{r}
excl_AI_n <- length(c("ID15", "ID21", "ID30", "ID53", "ID8")) # n removed, to exclude AI generated responses
excl_AI <- excl_dup - excl_AI_n # n left, after removing AI generated responses

excl_count <- excl_count %>%
  add_row(order = 8,
          description = "Removing suspected AI generated open text responses",
          n_removed = excl_AI_n,
          n_left = excl_AI)

excl_count

```


### Saving exclusions table:
```{r}
write_csv(excl_count, "data/excl_count.csv")

```



# Do the qual and quant datasets match? Because there should be the same ResponseIDs in each.
```{r}
# The qual data:
dat_qual <- read_csv("data/demos.csv")

dat_qual

# What IDs can we see for qual?
dat_qual_IDs <- dat_qual_IDs %>%
  filter(
    !Pseudonym %in% c(
      "Participant_15",
      "Participant_21",
      "Participant_30",
      "Participant_53",
      "Participant_8"
    )) # removing the responses flagged as AI generated from the dat_qual_IDs

dat_qual_IDs


# The quan data:
dat_comb_IDs <- dat_comb %>%
  group_by(Pseudonym) %>%
  count()

dat_comb_IDs


# DO THEY MATCH!?
# Use full_join because it keeps all observations in both data set x and y, so you'll see null results if there's a mismatch
dat_match <- full_join(
  x = dat_qual_IDs,
  y = dat_comb_IDs,
  by = c("Pseudonym")
)

dat_match


# Results:
## Well, both dat_comb and dat_qual_IDs have 56 responses each.
## dat_match also has 56 responses total and no null results

```

## Age:
```{r}
# demographics of the final sample

# age:

dat_age <- dat_comb %>%
  filter(Question == "age") %>%
  mutate(Answer = as.numeric(Answer))  # convert age to numeric


# the summary statistics:
summ_age <- dat_age %>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(Answer)) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    age_min = min(age),
    age_1st_Qu = quantile(age, 0.25, names = FALSE),
    age_med = median(age),
    age_3rd_Qu = quantile(age, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    age_max = max(age),
    age_mean = mean(age),
    age_sd = sd(age)
  )

summ_age

summary(dat_age) # min & max (for age range)


# Violin box-plot distribution of the ages:
plot_age <- ggplot(dat_age %>% mutate(group = "Age"), 
                   aes(x = group, y = Answer, fill = group)) +
  #
  ## Colouring quartiles in the background:
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, ymin = summ_age$age_min, xmax = Inf, ymax = summ_age$age_1st_Qu, fill = "grey0", alpha = 0.03) +
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, ymin = summ_age$age_1st_Qu, xmax = Inf, ymax = summ_age$age_med, fill = "grey25", alpha = 0.03) +
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, ymin = summ_age$age_med, xmax = Inf, ymax = summ_age$age_3rd_Qu, fill = "grey50", alpha = 0.03) +
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, ymin = summ_age$age_3rd_Qu, xmax = Inf, ymax = summ_age$age_max, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.03) +
  #
  ## Drawing the violin boxplot:
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0, fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE, fill = "white", colour = "black") +
  #
  ## Labels:
  scale_x_discrete(name = "", labels = c("Age Distribution")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Age (years)") +
  #
  ## Annotation(s):
  annotate("label", x = 1.3, y = summ_age$age_med,
    label = paste0(round(summ_age$age_med, 3), " years"),
    fill = "white", colour = "black")
  
plot_age


## To save plot_age as high-resolution PNG, remove the # from the following code:
ggsave("figures/plot_age.png", plot_age, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 120)

```


## Gender:
```{r}
# gender:

dat_gender <- dat_comb %>%
  filter(Question == "gender")


# the summary statistics:
summ_gender <- dat_gender %>%
  group_by(Answer) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  mutate(percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>% # one decimal place
  ungroup()

summ_gender


# Desired order for plot_gender:
order_gender <- c(
  "Female",
  "Male",
  "Non-binary"
)

summ_gender <- summ_gender %>%
  mutate(order = factor(Answer, levels = order_gender))


# Plot for gender proportions:
plot_gender <- summ_gender %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = order, y = n, fill = order)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, colour = "black", fill = "black") +
  labs(x = "Gender Identity",
       y = "Count") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_text(aes(x = order, y = n, label = n), nudge_y = 3) + # labels for columns
  scale_fill_grey(start = 1, end = 0) # to be colour-blind & black-white printing friendly

plot_gender


## To save plot_gender as high-resolution PNG, remove the # from the following code:
ggsave("figures/plot_gender.png", plot_gender, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 120)

```

### What category of neurodivergent?
```{r}
dat_neurod_specify <- dat_comb %>%
  filter(Question == c("neurodivergent_1_TEXT"))

# Saving this table so I can code it by hand to find out the count for e.g. N said Autism, Y said ADHD, etc.
write_csv(dat_neurod_specify, "data/dat_neurod_specify.csv")

```


BEWARE! You must MANUALLY recode the specific type of neurodivergence! It needs a human eye! The recoding is NOT automated because of the variation in how participants wrote about the same type of neurodivergence.

PLEASE date and name who recoded the data, if you decide to recode it yourself e.g. dat_neurod_specify_recoded-2026-08-20_bySaraEftekhari.csv

It's VERY IMPORTANT to NOT use a space BEFORE AND AFTER the commas when you're recoding.

```{r}
# Loading in the recoded neurodivergent categories:
dat_neurod_recoded <- read_csv("data/dat_neurod_specify_recoded-2026-08-20_bySaraEftekhari.csv")

dat_neurod_recoded


# Counting the types of neurodivergent categories (CO-OCCURANCE ALLOWED):
# the summary statistics:
summ_neurod_recoded <- dat_neurod_recoded %>%
  group_by(Recoding) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  filter(Recoding != "NA") %>% # removes the NA responses
  mutate(percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>% # one decimal place
  ungroup()

summ_neurod_recoded %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) # sorts from largest to smallest n


# Counting neurodivergent categories INDIVIDUALLY:
summ_neurod_recoded_indiv <- dat_neurod_recoded %>%
  separate_rows(Recoding, sep = ",") %>% # splits up the categories separated by a comma originally
  count(Recoding, name = "n") %>%
  filter(Recoding != "NA") %>% # removes the NA responses
  mutate(percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

summ_neurod_recoded_indiv %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) # sorts from largest to smallest n


# Saving count of neurodivergent categories:
write_csv(summ_neurod_recoded_indiv, "data/dat_neurod_count.csv")

```

```{r}
  mutate(Answer = recode(Answer,
```

```{r}
                         "Non-academic Use" = "Non-academic Use",

                         ))
```

```{r}
# Using the logic of "Within each use type, keep all tools whose count is greater than or equal to the 5th-highest count" i.e. it's top 5 tools but technically there will be more than 5 tools mentioned because some of the tools have a tied number of responses:

top_ac <- summ_tools_used %>% 
  filter(Answer == "Academic Use") %>%
  mutate(rank = dense_rank(desc(n))) %>% # dense_rank() is a dplyr ranking function that assigns the same rank to tied values
  filter(rank <= 5) %>%
  select(-rank) # keeps the top 5 counts for tools and includes any ties
```

# Counting tools used (aggregate count across Used types)
```{r}
# I'm collapsing the "Academic Use", "Non-academic Use", and "Academic and Non-academic Use" into one broad "Use" category, per participant, per tool. This is to count how many participants said they "Use" a tool, regardless of what use type that is.

## So this means grouping based on ResponseId and Description. It also means recoding the use types into one "Use" category.

## dat_ai_tools is the go-to table.

use_count <- dat_ai_tools %>%
  # To recode, %in% is an R operator that checks whether each value on the left appears in a set of values on the right, giving "TRUE" or "FALSE":
  mutate(
    Use = Answer %in% c(
      "Academic Use",
      "Non-academic Use",
      "Academic and Non-academic Use"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Only getting "Use" category:
  filter(Use == TRUE) %>%
  # Group by ResponseId and Description for grouping by participant and tool:
  group_by(ResponseId, Description) %>% # what tools respondents used
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # In the survey, participants could pick "Academic Use" AND/OR "Non-academic Use". If they picked both, this got recoded as "Academic and Non-academic Use". Meaning any participant left with just "Academic Use" or "Non-academic Use" means there was no other use type. As in, a participant whose response was left as "Academic Use" did NOT select "Non-academic Use". And vice versa. So in reality "Academic Use", "Non-academic Use", and "Academic and Non-academic Use" SHOULD all be mutually exclusive, meaning the n = 1 is the check you're looking in the n column of use_count.

  ## Which is exactly what we got! n = 1 for all!

  # Now we need to count each tool:
  group_by(Description) %>% # what tools respondents used
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # We should see 25 tools. 
  
  arrange(desc(n)) # sorts from largest to smallest n


use_count


# Save as a CSV:
write_csv(use_count, "data/use_count.csv")

```

## Summary stats of frequency
```{r}
summ_freq <- dat_freq %>%
  group_by(Question, Answer) %>% # type of use + frequency
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::complete(Question, Answer, fill = list(n = 0)) %>% # makes sure summarise doesn't drop any frequencies with a 0 count
  mutate(
    percentage = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1),
    Question = recode(Question,
                     "academic_frequency" = "Academic",
                     "nonacademic_frequenc" = "Non-academic",
                     .default = Question)
  ) # total sum(n) across all rows

summ_freq
```
